text:
Alex: anyone else seeing a burst of internal 502s around 02:05? traces point to service-to-service calls timing out during name resolution.
Mira: yep saw the same, p99 DNS resolve jumped to ~3.2s for a bunch of pods at 02:03 UTC :eyes: coreDNS logs show repeated `forwarding error: read udp: i/o timeout`.
Sam: ran quick checks from a node with the issue — node-local-dns answered but often with TC set so clients fallback to TCP. `dig @127.0.0.1 svc01.namespace.svc.cluster.local` returned `;; Truncated, retrying in TCP` frequently.
Juan: interesting — recall we have a mix of RDMA-enabled GPU nodes with MTU 9000 and standard nodes at 1500. If UDP fragments get lost on paths with different MTU, DNS responses can get truncated / retransmitted.
Katie: checked NIC stats on affected leaf: `ip -s -s link show dev ib0` shows RX errors and high frag reassembly drops. also `cat /proc/net/snmp` shows uptick in UDPInOverflows.
Mira: coreDNS is also under memory pressure on the master AZ; when it falls behind it forwards more, increasing packet size -> more chance of truncation.
Alex: quick mitigation we can try now: 1) increase node-local-dns TTL to 30s to reduce chattiness, 2) scale coreDNS from 2 -> 4 replicas in the AZ with spikes, 3) temporarily relax iptables conntrack timeout for DNS flows. Rolling canary for coredns scale first.
Sam: applying a local test patch: 
```
kubectl -n kube-system set resources deploy/coredns --replicas=4
# on nodes: sed -i 's/ttl: 5s/ttl: 30s/' /etc/kubelet-resolver.conf && systemctl restart node-local-dns
```
can confirm dig latency improves from ~3s -> ~200ms on test node.
Juan: long-term fix: normalize MTU or ensure fragmentation/DF behaviour is consistent. Path MTU discovery failing with some RDMA offloads has bitten us before. I suspect TCP fallback masking the real issue.
Katie: also saw tcpdump on a path where DNS response was 2000 bytes -> fragmented into 1500-sized UDP packets, fragment #2 was dropped somewhere (likely a switch or kernel with GRO/GSO mismatch).
Mira: FYI adding EDNS0 buffer-size tweak to allow bigger UDP might make things worse if fragments are dropped — better to eliminate fragmentation.
Alex: agreed. Plan: short term = TTL bump + coreDNS scale (done in canary), mid term = audit MTU across fabric and schedule kernel/firmware update for RDMA NICs, long term = enforce consistent MTU in provisioning pipeline.
Sam: opening infra ticket with logs/traces + suggested node pool reboot window. I'll capture a tcpdump snippet and route MTU hunch to networking team.
InfraBot: automated alert acknowledged for ticket INFRA-1242 (DNS-resolve-frag-mtu).
deploy-bot: canary rollout: coredns replicas -> 4 applied to zone-a; 3/3 pods ready; monitoring p99.
Katie: after canary p99 reduced ~18% cluster-wide, but we still see isolated 1-2% failures on the largest GPU pools (RDMA). recommend scheduled maintenance for those nodes.
Juan: I'll coordinate with platform to freeze GPU provisioning during the reboot window to avoid capacity churn.
Mira: thanks all — leaving traces and sample tcpdump in the ticket (INFRA-1242). :thumbsup:
Alex: great, let's reconvene after the reboot window and confirm whether the MTU normalization fixed the remaining tails.
